title: Which parts of the genome: regions associated with fin or wing proportion
simplification_warning: "The genes that code for wings" is a simplification. Neither a flying fish wing (an enlarged pectoral fin) nor a bat wing has a gene of its own. What the sources identify are regions ASSOCIATED with fin or wing proportion: a few protein-coding substitutions, genes evolving at changed rates, and, mostly, non-coding regulatory elements (accelerated or constrained conserved non-coding elements, enhancers). Association is not causation, and only a few have been tested functionally.

CNEs_associated_with_focal_genes.source: Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.5082978 (record 5082979), medaka_cne_great.txt: assembled CNEs assigned to neighbouring protein-coding genes by the GREAT rule, MEDAKA1 coordinates
CNEs_associated_with_focal_genes.limit: These counts cover ALL captured CNEs near each gene, not only accelerated ones; the accelerated subset is reported only as GO enrichments (sheets K and M). A count of 0 can mean the gene ID used (Ensembl release 116) did not exist in the MEDAKA1 annotation the file uses (tbx5a, fgf10a), or that Ensembl has no medaka orthologue (kcnh2a); it does not mean the gene has no regulatory elements.

bats.what: regulatory regions and programmes implicated in bat wing development, from Europe PMC searches (queries and hit counts in sequences/calls.json; each entry paraphrases the fetched abstract)
bats.reading: Every bat entry is regulatory (enhancers, accelerated non-coding regions, expression programmes); none is a protein-coding change. That matches the flying-fish side, where accelerated non-coding elements far outnumber convergent coding substitutions.

regions.finding: Replacing the mouse Prx1 limb enhancer with the orthologous bat sequence raised Prx1 expression in developing forelimb bones and gave significantly longer forelimbs; deleting the mouse enhancer left limb length normal, showing regulatory redundancy.

cite.title: Regulatory divergence modifies limb length between mammals.

regions.region: BAR116, telomeric to the HoxD cluster (one of 166 bat accelerated regions overlapping limb enhancer marks)
regions.kind: bat-accelerated conserved non-coding region acting as enhancer
regions.finding: 166 bat accelerated regions overlap H3K27ac/p300 limb peaks; five Myotis lucifugus BARs drove limb expression in mice. The Myotis BAR116 sequence gave robust forelimb expression at E12.5 where the mouse sequence gave none, matching high-forelimb Hoxd10-Hoxd11 expression in Miniopterus bat embryos.

regions.finding: A specific fibroblast population expressing MEIS2 and TBX3 gives rise to the chiropatagium; ectopic MEIS2+TBX3 in mouse distal limb activated wing-associated genes and caused digit fusion.
